Canford School - Independent Boarding & Day School in Dorset
Canford school pupils have achieved excellent A Level results across the board with 25% of all grades at A* and 87% at A* to B. This compares with 9.7% at A* and 55.8% A*-B nationally.
Canford School has been recognised as one of the leading schools in the country following the publication of its latest Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) report, which highlights a "significant strength" in the development of pupil leadership.
Canford School is proud and honoured to learn the news that it has been ranked top independent school in the South of England in the 2025 Independent School Parent industry awards.
A school community where all are inspired to explore, empowered to express and challenged to excel.
To build a community of open-minded people who are motivated to embrace learning in all its forms, and committed to making a difference to their own lives, and to the lives of others. Our exceptional education grants freedom to grow and creates opportunities for all to explore, to express and to excel.

School Structure and Location
Founded in 1923, Canford is a full boarding school - there is no flexi or weekly boarding. Day pupils take advantage of the 24/7 school environment and can join boarders for activities and events during the evenings and at weekends. The size of the school - currently 650 pupils - means that we can offer and compete against other schools in sporting, academic and cultural activities but also ensure every pupil is known and valued as an individual. The beauty of our campus with 250 acres of landscaped grounds is well known as among the most special in the UK, and our proximity to the Dorset coast offers a unique and inspirational place in which to live and work.
We offer a top quality British boarding school education achieving excellence for all our pupils across academic, co-curricular and pastoral care and are proud of our recognised position among the leading independent schools in the country.

Canford is a school of opportunities. We want pupils to be excited about learning, both through academic challenge and a rich and extensive co-curricular programme which offers a very wide range of options for creativity and self-discovery.

Results and Careers
We are ambitious for Canfordians to achieve their very best outcomes academically to enable them to follow their chosen future career and work pathways. Canford is proud of its high quality teachers who are specialists in their field with a genuine passion and enthusiasm for their subject.
Our academic results are ranked consistently top among co-educational schools in the South West region by The Sunday Times Parent Power (2023-2026), we were awarded Public School of the Year by Tatler and Boarding School of the Year by ISP and as The Good Schools Guide describes us "With its first rate teaching, stunning setting and innovative ideas, Canford is definitely top of its game."

A Welcoming Community
Everyone who joins Canford becomes a member of our vibrant, welcoming community. All who are part of Canford are part of it for life, and our community extends beyond our pupils, staff, families and alumni to all we have links with through our community action projects living locally, regionally, nationally and internationally.
The Christian faith has been at the heart of Canford’s spiritual identity since the school was founded in 1923. In 21st-century multicultural Britain, we honour these Christian foundations while welcoming and valuing pupils from all faith backgrounds and those with no religious faith. The spiritual aim of the school is to support pupils in exploring questions of meaning, purpose and belief, nurturing faith where it exists and encouraging reflection and curiosity in all.

We Are
What makes a Canfordian?
Our vision is to offer every pupil the chance to explore their talents, to express their personalities and views and to be the very best they can be. Powerful statements borne out through our pupil outcomes.
Every pupil is encouraged to explore, with the coherence of a Canford education across both academic and co-curricular elements promoting lifelong personal development and self-understanding.
Pursuing goals without arrogance or complacency brings meaningful success.
We challenge members of our community to be energetic and resilient in pursuit of their goals but honest and grateful for fulfilment of them.
Canford is welcoming to all regardless of socio-economic background, race, religion, physical ability, gender or sexuality.
Through our programmes we enhance and enrich experiences for all across our School who are able to express their individuality, excel in the global community and explore the rich history of our world.
We want out pupils to challenge existing wisdom, to create, to share their passions, views and opinions.
Being principled and strong, yet reflective and tolerant, takes courage.

Drama
The 300 seat Layard Theatre is home to the busy Drama Department, which currently has around sixty pupils studying Drama and Theatre Arts at GCSE and A Level. The theatre is a dynamic space - an exciting environment in which to study and explore both practically and academically. It is a hub for creativity.
Drama at Canford continues to grow and inspire, providing opportunities for students of all ages to explore performance, design and directing. Students enjoy a rich calendar of productions, a range of co-curricular activities, and benefit from a programme of visiting theatre professionals. There are also regular opportunities to collaborate with the local community - whether through outreach projects, shared performances, or partnerships with nearby arts organisations. The department is vibrant, imaginative, and committed to nurturing every student's creative ambitions.
A wide-ranging programme of school productions enables all students to get involved with the theatrical life of the school, whether on stage or behind the scenes. Last year’s whole school musical, Just So by George Stiles and Anthony Drewe, brought Rudyard Kipling’s whimsical tales to life through months of dedicated rehearsal. Featuring a cast of 35 pupils and a live orchestra, the production celebrated the power of storytelling with colourful characters and imaginative staging. This year we are exploring a diverse range of theatrical styles and voices, with a season featuring The Addams Family by Andrew Lippa, Accidental Death of an Anarchist by Dario Fo, The 39 Steps by Patrick Barlow and The Terrible Infants by Oliver Lansley. Directed by the drama department, these productions aim to demonstrate the outstanding range of talent at Canford.
A large number of pupils participate in the Spring and Summer Productions, exploring contemporary and classical texts to create exciting work for a live theatre audience. Alongside nurturing and developing performance skills, these productions also offer the chance for those interested in design and stage management to work in collaboration with our technical theatre manager, performing arts technicians, choreographer and wardrobe supervisor to visually create the production.
An array of studio productions takes place each year, directed by students. The focus on directing begins in Shells (Year 9), where pupils start to explore theatre production as part of their academic studies. After selecting short excerpts from plays or writing their own original works, pupils direct their pieces for performance - with recent choices including Road and The Frost Report.
Enrichment Programmes
We regularly welcome a range of visiting speakers into school for talks and workshops, broadening pupils’ perspectives and offering insight into careers in drama and theatre. Trips and visits encourage pupils to experience the UK’s vibrant theatre scene. As well as enriching the studies of those taking drama, all pupils can participate in the department's initiative, Friday Foyer - a monthly pop-up performance evening held in the theatre foyer. Open to all, it offers a relaxed and supportive space where students can showcase monologues, short scenes or songs they’ve been working on, or simply come along to enjoy the performances with refreshments and friends.

Music
Music at Canford enjoys a high profile within the busy school life. We hope that when pupils leave Canford they will continue to pursue their music-making independently having gained sufficient skills whilst at school to enable them to sing in choirs, play in bands or orchestras or just to enjoy playing at home as a hobby. For some, further professional training will beckon and we know that the rounded and high-level musical education provided at Canford will also prove an excellent foundation for a music degree or a Conservatoire course.
The Music department welcomes musicians of all abilities who have enthusiasm to learn. All those who learn an orchestral or band instrument are encouraged to join an appropriate ensemble in this lively, ambitious and successful department. Many musicians will be in more than one ensemble, allowing them to gain experience of different music, styles and instrumental combinations. A level and GCSE music are popular choices, but involvement in ensembles is open to all, whether or not they have opted to pursue the academic subject. The skills and understanding acquired in music are broad, ranging from subject-specific technical knowledge, through the practical aspects of composition and performance, to ‘life-skills’ such as teamwork, self-discipline and motivation.
The department has its own purpose-built facility next to the Layard Theatre, with a concert hall seating a maximum of 300, able to contain the largest ensembles with an acoustic and ambience that suits solo performance and informal concerts. It has a Steinway piano and a three manual digital Allen Organ. There are a range of further teaching, rehearsal and practice rooms.

Approximately a third of the pupils in the school learn a musical instrument, and many learn two or three. We have pupils at all levels, from beginner through to diploma and beyond, and our visiting teachers are highly qualified, often enjoying a performing career alongside their work as teachers. Many pupils, guided by their teachers, will choose to pursue music exams and results are excellent. It is notable that pupils see Grade 8 or a diploma before they leave as a ‘goal’ and work hard to achieve this: as a result, we usually have at least 25 instruments being played at or beyond this standard in the school at any one time.
Our larger ensembles include groups such as the orchestra or wind orchestra, as well as the ever-popular jazz band, whilst our choirs range from the near 70-strong chapel choir to the auditioned chamber choir of just 16 pupils. Chamber music groups offer scholars and more advanced musicians the opportunity to explore further exciting challenges and repertoire.

Canford offers a number of awards at both 13+ and 16+ for talented musicians. Whilst there are a great number of pupils in the school who love music and play instruments, music scholars are at the very heart of our music-making. We offer all of our musicians a variety of opportunities, but are keen to tailor our provision to each individual, and this is especially true of music scholars. In addition to leading our larger ensembles, music scholars may participate in more advanced chamber groups, perform solos more frequently, and participate in masterclasses with visiting musicians.
Whilst scholars are fully involved in many musical ensembles and choirs, the way that the Canford day is structured, and the ethos of the school allows them also to pursue other talents and interests.
For all those considering a music scholarship application, early contact with the music department is advised, and the Director of Music, William Ings, is always happy to meet with parents and potential music scholars and to hold pre-auditions.
For details regarding Music scholarships please contact our Admissions team.

Music
Music at Canford enjoys a high profile within the busy school life. We hope that when pupils leave Canford they will continue to pursue their music-making independently having gained sufficient skills whilst at school to enable them to sing in choirs, play in bands or orchestras or just to enjoy playing at home as a hobby. For some, further professional training will beckon and we know that the rounded and high-level musical education provided at Canford will also prove an excellent foundation for a music degree or a Conservatoire course.
The Music department welcomes musicians of all abilities who have enthusiasm to learn. All those who learn an orchestral or band instrument are encouraged to join an appropriate ensemble in this lively, ambitious and successful department. Many musicians will be in more than one ensemble, allowing them to gain experience of different music, styles and instrumental combinations. A level and GCSE music are popular choices, but involvement in ensembles is open to all, whether or not they have opted to pursue the academic subject. The skills and understanding acquired in music are broad, ranging from subject-specific technical knowledge, through the practical aspects of composition and performance, to ‘life-skills’ such as teamwork, self-discipline and motivation.
The department has its own purpose-built facility next to the Layard Theatre, with a concert hall seating a maximum of 300, able to contain the largest ensembles with an acoustic and ambience that suits solo performance and informal concerts. It has a Steinway piano and a three manual digital Allen Organ. There are a range of further teaching, rehearsal and practice rooms.

Approximately a third of the pupils in the school learn a musical instrument, and many learn two or three. We have pupils at all levels, from beginner through to diploma and beyond, and our visiting teachers are highly qualified, often enjoying a performing career alongside their work as teachers. Many pupils, guided by their teachers, will choose to pursue music exams and results are excellent. It is notable that pupils see Grade 8 or a diploma before they leave as a ‘goal’ and work hard to achieve this: as a result, we usually have at least 25 instruments being played at or beyond this standard in the school at any one time.
Our larger ensembles include groups such as the orchestra or wind orchestra, as well as the ever-popular jazz band, whilst our choirs range from the near 70-strong chapel choir to the auditioned chamber choir of just 16 pupils. Chamber music groups offer scholars and more advanced musicians the opportunity to explore further exciting challenges and repertoire.

Art
Canford has a thriving Art department and the Art School is a place where pupils can react creatively to the world around them. We encourage individuals to find areas of the subject that interest them and to work with confidence and ambition, through a wide range of exciting projects, workshops, lectures, exhibitions and trips.
Pupils and staff are encouraged to produce creative, diverse and personal work that challenges expectations of what can be produced in a school environment. The results are work that is of the highest quality.
Students work within the broad boundary of Art, Craft and Design in media such as painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, illustration, mixed media, fashion, film, textiles, photography and installation work. Many will cross over between a number of these disciplines. The department runs an exciting programme where visiting contemporary artists discuss their work and run practical workshops. These engaging events promote diverse and sophisticated responses. The studios are open for all pupils well beyond the working day including a majority of weekends. Exhibitions and trips ensure pupils are aware of the subject beyond Canford and a large number choose to continue on to high profile Universities to study fine art, design, history of art and architecture. Study visits take place in term time and during the holidays and include New York, Berlin and Cornwall.
We teach to the Eduqas A Level Art and Design course. The style of the course is felt to be a strong foundation for Art college, with pupils able to produce more ambitious portfolios and work on a larger scale.

Canford School praised for exceptional pupil leadership in ISI Inspection
Watch our 'A Team' inspired film highlighting the 'significant strength' of our Pupil Leadership
Canford School has been recognised as one of the leading schools in the country following the publication of its latest Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) report, which highlights a “significant strength” in the development of pupil leadership.
The inspection, which took place last term, resulted in an exceptionally positive report across all areas of school life. We are keen to encourage people to read the report in full, reflecting our confidence in the inspectors’ findings and our pride in the whole-school community.
Of particular note is the inspection team’s award of a “significant strength” for pupil leadership, an accolade reserved for very few schools with areas of excellence that really stand out. Inspectors praised the way Canford empowers its pupils, recognising leadership at all levels as a defining feature of the school’s culture and ethos.
This recognition is seen as a testament not only to the pupils themselves, but also to the dedication and commitment of staff who support and nurture leadership at every level.
To mark the achievement, the school held a celebratory lunch for pupils and staff, reflecting Canford’s strong sense of community and shared success. From national awards and outstanding examination results to inspection outcomes, the school continues to celebrate incredible collective achievements.
The report places Canford firmly among the very best schools in the country, reinforcing its reputation for excellence and its commitment to developing confident, capable, and values-driven young leaders.
Headmaster, Chris Wheeler, said,
It is wonderful to see Canford recognised for so many of its strengths. The Inspection team were engaged, thorough and really took time to understand us. Our pupils are the engine room of the school and drive one another’s achievements, so it was a pleasure to see the inspectors describing our work in pupil leadership as a "significant strength".
Deputy Head Pastoral, Richard Redwood, said,
What stands out most in this report is the way our pupils look after one another as they grow into leaders. Their willingness to step forward for their peers reflects a pastoral culture where every young person feels valued, supported and empowered to make a positive difference.
Deputy Head Academic, Ieuan Weir, said,
I’m incredibly proud of our community. When dedicated teachers and pupils unite with care, purpose and belief, they spark excellence that rises far beyond the sum of its parts. We have a culture where collaboration turns effort into achievement.
The full ISI Inspection report can be viewed here:

Careers Planning and Outcomes
Everything we do at Canford is aimed at preparing pupils for their life when they leave the school, developing transferable skills and knowledge as well as values and beliefs in order for them to lead fulfilling lives in whatever they decide to do. A key role of the school in general and the Careers and Higher Education department in particular, is in helping pupils identify their motivations, strengths and areas for development and providing information, advice and support as they try to identify the right options and the best direction they might take after Sixth Form. We aim to help them develop and recognise their non-academic as well as academic skills and enable them to demonstrate them from a variety of activities they will inevitably become involved with while at school and then help them access opportunities to put these attributes into practice.

Canford has a deserved reputation for academic excellence and our external results at A Level and GCSE lead the way locally, regionally and nationally. We are consistently ranked No.1 by The Sunday Times Parent Power report among independent co-educational boarding schools in the South West. On average in the past three years, over 30% of all A Level grades have been at A* and over 65% at A*/A, while at GCSE nearly 30% of all examinations have been graded 9 (A*+) and three quarters 9-7 (A*/A).
Such results have enabled our Upper Sixth leavers to move on to top universities on a wide variety of courses, with over 80% taking up places at Russell Group/Sunday Times Top 12 institutions each year. 39 places at Oxbridge and 38 places to Medical Schools, scholarships to US universities, degree apprenticeships with leading corporates and places at Music Conservatoires and Art Institutes are among the choices of our leavers in the past 5 years. Our tailored, individual careers support ensures that every pupil has the best opportunity to achieve their aspirations and future career path ambitions.

The Good Schools Guide
Canford school pupils have achieved excellent A Level results across the board with 25% of all grades at A* and 87% at A* to B. This compares with 9.7% at A* and 55.8% A*-B nationally.
Amongst many amazing results for the whole cohort there were some particular achievements of Canford school pupils this year include:
Headmaster Chris Wheeler said:
"My congratulations and thanks go to every member of the year group, to our dedicated staff, and to parents for the support and encouragement they provide."
"Canford is a school driven by culture – a place where we believe that hard work results in success and this year's A level results are further evidence of – and testament to – that belief."
"We have invested significantly in the Sixth Form at Canford, including outstanding new teaching and residential facilities, which provide even greater opportunities for collaboration, independence and leadership, helping our pupils bridge the gap between school and the wider world.”
The majority of Canford school leavers are choosing to head to university with 88% of places to Russell Group/Sunday Times Top 12 institutions, including places confirmed at Oxbridge. From a highly aspirational set of offers, 90 pupils are moving on to their first-choice university destination. Those who aren’t heading to university include pupils who have accepted places at prestigious creative arts institutions, apprenticeships, and at international universities. This reflects the increasing variety of paths that Canford pupils embark on after leaving school and is testament to the school’s commitment to ensuing its pupils are genuinely real world ready.
Canford's Upper Sixth pupils celebrated another year of outstanding A Level achievement. Huge congratulations to this talented and dedicated year group who surpassed last year’s grades at the top levels and continued the school’s reputation for consistent top quality academic outcomes.
In terms of Canford’s headline statistics:
There were strong performances across arts, science and humanities, with at least two thirds of all Chemistry, Classical Civilisation, Computing, Further Maths, Geography, German, Latin, Music, Physics and Religious Studies papers awarded A*/A grades.
Among schools across the South of England, Canford’s A*/A results, at 57.6%, were once again over double those seen overall across the South West (27%) and continue to remain competitive against the more selective schools in the London (32.1%) and South East regions (31.2%). Canford also again outperformed the independent school sector averages, with the Canford A*/A of 57.6% representing a year on year increase in 2025 against a fall to average 48.4% among all independent schools compared with last year.
In terms of numbers within the Upper Sixth cohort:
A headline national statistic this year was that the proportion of pupils gaining 3A*s dropped in 2025, with 1.3% (3,890) of the 281,800 students in England achieving this. Once more, the efforts of Canfordians have shone forth compared with this national measure, with 13 of our pupils gaining at least 3A*s or better in 2025 representing 10% of the 131 Upper Sixth cohort.
These results are testament to the hard work and commitment of this talented year group. What is even more impressive is that these top-quality academic outcomes have been achieved within a broad and balanced school life. Our pupils achieve their very best and to their highest standards not only within the classroom but while also taking full advantage of the huge range of opportunities beyond it. This is a hallmark of life at Canford, with our multi-talented pupils combining their top results with, amongst many other things, Army scholarships, Gold Duke of Edinburgh Awards, distinctions in Maths Olympiads, music diplomas and high-level sporting achievements. Examination results are only one part of the picture of the life of a Canfordian, reflecting our school vision for every individual pupil to be nurtured by both staff and peers, to enable them to successfully ‘explore, express and excel’ in all elements of their education within our supportive school community.
A level Results by Subject 2025
Our Upper Sixth Canfordians excelled in this year’s A Level examinations. A quarter of all grades, 25%, were at the top grade A* with over half of all grades, 54%, at A*/A, 83% at A*/B and 96% A*/C, with strong performances across arts, science and humanities subjects. Once again Canford has significantly outperformed the national overall grade statistics which saw 9.3% of all grades at A*, 27.8% A*/A and 76% A*-C. Regionally Canford results were double those seen overall at A*/A across the South West and have also again outperformed the independent sector averages.
These results are testament to the hard work and commitment of this talented year group. Forty pupils gained straight A*/A grades, 12 with 3 or more A*s and a further 15 with at least 2A*/A grades. Breadth of opportunity is a hallmark of life at Canford, and like so many of our multi-talented pupils, these top performers took advantage of the many co-curricular options open to them, resulting in Army scholarships, Gold Duke of Edinburgh Awards, distinctions in Maths Olympiads, music diplomas and high level sporting achievements.
A level results 2024
Canford’s Upper Sixth pupils excelled once again in their A Level and Pre-U examinations, with 31% of all papers graded A*, 66% A*-A, 89% A*-B and 99% A*-C. These results are among the highest in the school’s 100 year history: a fine achievement in a year where the percentage of top grades has fallen nationally back to pre-Covid levels. By comparison, overall figures across England saw 8.6% of all examinations graded A*, 26.5% A*-A, 52.7% A*-B and 75.4% A*-C. According to Ofqual’s average statistics, independent schools saw 18.7% of all examinations graded A* and 47.4% graded A*-A. Across schools in our South West region the A*-A figure was 26.3%. Canfordians significantly outperformed both across the sector and across the country.
Excellence was evident in results across the range of Arts, Science and Humanities subjects at A Level, while in Pre-U, D1 grades (beyond an A* at A Level) were achieved in Art and French, with over a third of all papers in Art, French, German and Spanish awarded D1-D2 grades (A* at A Level). 83% of all Extended Project Qualifications (EPQs worth half an A Level) were graded A*-A.
Sixteen Canfordians were awarded straight A*s or D1/D2 grades, twelve gained at least 4 A*/As and 58 pupils, over 40% of the cohort, were awarded at least 3 A*/A grades. Like so many of our pupils, these top performers are multi-talented, with their additional successes including GB swimming and Performance Level netball selection, ABRSM Music diplomas, Grade VIII distinctions and original musical direction and commendation in National essay competitions.
A level results 2023
Pre-U results 2023 (art, french, german, spanish)
We were absolutely delighted with the outstanding results achieved by Canfordians sitting A Level and Pre-U examinations this summer, with 40.9% of all grades awarded A*, 75.1% A*/A and 92.6% A*/B. Nationally, 14.5% of all grades awarded were A* and 35.9% A*/A, while in the Independent Schools sector overall, the average was 28.7% for A* and 58% for A*/A.
The last few years have been very difficult for teachers, pupils and their families and exam boards alike. Comparisons with recent exam years need to be considered in context as the landscape and factors which affected the award of Centre Assessed Grades of 2020 (CAGs) and Teacher Assessed Grades of 2021 (TAGs) were very different. The charts below indicate the comparison with the last time examinations were sat in 2019.
Despite reports that results nationally are markedly lower than the 2020 and 2021 grades, it is notable that our A* grades are 16.9% higher, A*/A 4.1% higher and A*/B 1.5% higher than the CAGs of 2020. Indeed, our results today are only marginally lower than last year’s TAGs.
There was excellence across all faculties, with Arts, Sciences and Humanities all recording high percentages of top grades. At least 80% of all Music, Maths, Further Maths, Economics, Geography, Physics, Computing and Chemistry papers were awarded A*/A grades, while in Pre-U there were D1s (beyond an A* at A Level) in French and Spanish with 100% of all German papers graded D1-D2 (A*/A). Three quarters of all Extended Project Qualifications (EPQs) were graded A*/A. Twenty pupils were awarded three A* grades and five pupils gained four A*s.
A Level Results 2022
Pre-U Results 2022 (Art, French, German, Spanish)
It is not possible, nor fair, to compare the 2021 results with previous years because the method of assessment was so different and, crucially, there were no national norm standardised examinations.
However, we can be confident that we provided our pupils with the best opportunities to demonstrate their learning, we were thorough and fair in our methods and we are delighted with and proud of our pupils’ achievements.
It is not possible, nor fair, to compare the 2020 results with previous years because the method of assessment was so different and, crucially, there were no national norm standardised examinations.
However, we can be confident that we provided our pupils with the best opportunities to demonstrate their learning, we were thorough and fair in our methods and we are delighted with and proud of our pupils’ achievements.

A Level Results 2018
Pre-U Results 2018 (Art, French, German, Spanish)
A Level Results 2017

Following the excellent achievements of our Upper Sixth where we saw 31% of all grades awarded A* and Canford’s results among the top co-educational boarding schools in the country, we were equally delighted for our Fifth Formers who recorded wonderful success in their GCSEs, again some of the very best results in the school’s history.
This year, both nationally and in independent schools, overall grades fell back to 2019 levels, yet Canford bucked this trend with higher grades in 2023 versus 2019 across the board. A quarter (24.8%) of all Canford grades were awarded the top grade of 9, widely acknowledged as beyond an A*, compared to 4.9% nationally. Almost half (48.5%) of all Canford papers were awarded the two highest grades 9-8 (A*), while 72.8% of all grades were 9-7 (A*-A) compared with a national overall figure of 21.6%, 46.6% in independent schools and 20.8% across the South West region. 99.8% of Canford GCSEs were graded 9-4 (A*-C) compared with 67.8% nationally and 90.1% in independent schools.
Results of the highest quality were seen across the Arts, Sciences and Humanities, with at least three quarters of all Canford Chemistry, Classical Greek, Design, English, Geography, German, History, Maths, Philosophy and Theology and Physics graded 9-7.
Fifteen pupils (13% of the year group) were awarded a clean sweep of 9-8 (A*) grades, a third of our cohort gained an impressive average of grade 8 (A*) or higher in all their examinations, and 61% of the year group gained an average of grade 7 (A*-A) or higher. Not only have our Fifth Form achieved highly academically, as a year group they have also grasped the wide array of co-curricular opportunities we offer with enthusiasm and a great deal of personal and collective success. Their individual and combined contributions to the school across all areas such as sport, the creative and performing arts, CCF and broader community life have been very significant.
Just as for our Sixth Form, we were so proud of all our pupils for their excellent performances at GCSE. 33.6% of all Canford grades were awarded the very highest grade 9, compared to the national average of 6.6%, while 58.5% of all grades were 9-8 (A*) compared to the national average of 15.1%. 79.4% of all grades awarded to Canfordians were 9-7 (A*-A), compared with a national overall figure of 26.3% and 53% in independent schools on average. 99.7% of Canford GCSEs were graded 9-4 (A*-C) compared with 73% nationally and 92.5% in independent schools.

Our History
Canford School was founded in 1923, but occupies buildings with a rich history stretching back to before the Norman Conquest. The first written record of Canford Manor is an entry in the Domesday Book in the 1080s. The only medieval part still standing, known as John O'Gaunt's, dates from around 1400 and is now used by the school debating society, as a general meeting room and for formal dinners.
In 1846, the Canford estate was bought by Sir Josiah John Guest, a wealthy steel works owner, and his wife Lady Charlotte for £354,000, a tidy sum in mid-nineteenth century. The Guests engaged Sir Charles Barry (best known as architect of the Houses of Parliament) to remodel the house. The most obvious additions were the imposing Tower and the Great Hall, now used as the school’s dining hall, which features an elaborately decorated high roof, a huge stone fireplace decorated with the Guest family’s coats of arms, mosaic figures from Canford’s history and stained glass windows.
Barry also designed Nineveh Court, an addition on the eastern side of the main building, built to house the Assyrian treasures which Lady Charlotte Guest's archaeologist cousin, Henry Layard, brought back from the Middle East. Most of the collection was sold by Guest’s grandson, Lord Wimborne, in 1919 and is now in the Metropolitan Museum in New York. Happily for the school, some smaller items were overlooked, to be rediscovered in the 1950s, when they were sold for £14,000. The one remaining bas-relief, from the palace of Ashurnasirpal II, was examined at that time and declared to be a plaster copy. The visit to the school of an American historian, Professor John Malcolm Russell, in 1992 led to the amazing discovery that this bas-relief was genuine and it was sold at Christie’s in 1994 for £7.7 million, a record sum for an item of ancient art. The school has invested this windfall wisely, setting aside a substantial amount for scholarships and bursaries and funds towards the building of a new sports hall, theatre and girls’ boarding house.

School Archivist - Jessica Bichard
The Archivist, Jessica Bichard, is keen to add to the school collection and therefore is always happy to receive Canford memorabilia. Should you have any items relating to your time at the school that you no longer wish to keep, please either send them to Jess at the school or contact her to make arrangements. She would also welcome reminiscences from former staff and pupils about their time at Canford and about any memorable people. If you are sending photographs it would be helpful if names could be attached where possible.
